browser.emccVersion: emcc (Emscripten gcc/clang-like replacement + linker emulating GNU ld) 6.0.9 (4e4223852a0835923411059a3929907d7df1232e)

patches.reason: Execute the model-reader closure inline for single-threaded Emscripten, preserving native/pthread behavior.
Lower supported group-normalization layouts to existing NORM where equivalent, with CPU reference tests.
Do not misreport maxBufferSize as total/free GPU memory. Image callers must supply an explicit budget when live capacity is unknown.
Read unsplit GGUF metadata without whole-file size_t accumulation; preserve 64-bit file positions, validate metadata and leave tensor payloads lazy.
Keep a 64-bit logical metadata cursor; avoid tellg buffer invalidation and repeated FileReaderSync reads while retaining bounded skips and file checks.
Keep safetensors file positions 64-bit, bound/validate metadata and local shard paths, and load complete standard GGUF shard groups without file conversion.
Avoid an in-place Qwen timestep SiLU alias across a BF16 CPU matmul / WebGPU activation boundary. Preserve weights and arithmetic; no profile fallback or dtype conversion.
Report bounded allocation-time BF16 weight matmul placement through existing logs, without changing graph execution or reading tensor contents.
Convert only original BF16 parameters before WebGPU allocation to caller-selected F32 (default) or F16, preserving source files and other weight types.
Replace recursive graph-parent traversal with a heap-backed DFS stack, preserving order, compute flags and operand use counts for deep image graphs.
Give browser 3D convolution bias additions their own output when CPU convolution and WebGPU addition use different backends, preserving arithmetic and parameter types.
Use an equivalent supported 2D direct convolution for a single full-depth 3D window instead of CPU fallback, without changing parameter types or allocating a full im2col volume.

Expose idle on-demand runtime, borrowed configuration and separately labelled memory bookkeeping snapshots without adding generation-path instrumentation or GPU synchronization; own the omitted audio-encoder configuration path.

Add explicit default-off, bounded graph-stage logs to distinguish preparation, scheduler reserve including sync, weights, allocation, input copy and execution without extra native timing, graph walks or GPU synchronization.
Preserve external tensor address metadata while measuring scheduler graphs; avoid invalid sentinel alignment in WebGPU GET_ROWS support checks without changing weights or backend policy.
Lower unsupported multi-frame 1x1x1 convolution to supported matrix and contiguous operations without im2col expansion; retain direct, precision, single-frame and rejected-backend paths.
H3 video output allocation is checked and cancellation-safe; completed frames are published together without an extra float crop, and unused frame outputs are released.
Allow finite 180-second queue completion for video graphs that exceed 30 seconds; retain independent 30-second map/event deadlines and all wait/callback failure checks.
Wait for submitted work, maps and events without an application wall-clock deadline; keep wait/callback failures and per-recording event ownership.
Lower zero-history single-image causal convolution to a packed temporal slice only when the selected backend supports the candidate; preserve circular/history/video fallbacks.

Keep structural Anima zero-padding mass with explicit sinks and reuse immutable sampling conditions through RunnerCache; remove when upstream provides equivalent scoped ownership, invalidation and fallback contracts.
Copy compatible same-device tensor ranges directly on the WebGPU queue; preserve synchronous and asynchronous contracts and retain fallback for unsupported ranges.
Allocate cache destinations before queuing same-device copies, then complete once before publishing ownership; preserve host/strided fallbacks and failure lifetimes.

Bound rejected convolution expansions and manual attention scores using existing WebGPU operations; require every introduced compute node to be supported, retaining precision, masks, sinks and original fallbacks.
Report an opt-in compute-operation placement histogram and current rejection counts without tensor names, readbacks, extra synchronization or execution-time claims.

Stage aligned per-kernel uniform parameters in a bounded host mirror and flush once before each existing WebGPU command submission; retain queue order, throttling, graph boundaries, bindings and slot lifetimes. Remove when the pinned upstream provides equivalent batching.

Avoid a queue completion registration when a runner or graph-cut cache has no new outputs; retain waits for every non-empty capture and exceptional copy exit. Segment computation keeps its own completion boundary.

Index the softmax private cache by lane iteration, use guarded storage/cache loads instead of eager select, and retain the same per-lane sum/reduction/precision. Remove when pinned upstream supplies equivalent bounds-safe cache use.

Fuse unmasked manual attention scaling into an admitted WebGPU softmax AFTER F32 score accumulation, without changing Q/K, masks, sinks, CPU behavior or Flash settings. Remove when upstream avoids the score-scale pass with equivalent admission and numerical contracts.

Share one graph-local position-matrix preparation across Qwen 2.1 WebGPU Q/K consumers. No persistent pointer-keyed cache or new numerical operation. Remove when upstream shares or fuses the equivalent RoPE position work with graph-cut-safe ownership.

Share graph-local Qwen Image 2.1 modulation, borrow read-only contiguous spans and select already-supported F32 SwiGLU; preserve 008 CPU/unsupported paths, graph-cut lifetimes and an immutable context A/B opt-out. Remove when upstream supplies equivalent guarded work reduction.

Extend existing opt-in placement logs with bounded WebGPU operation/subtype counts and largest logical output; no readback, timestamps, tensor names, new synchronization or GPU-time/VRAM claims. Remove when upstream supplies equivalent allocation metadata.

Dispatch row normalization, fused RMS multiply, softmax and GLU in a checked 2D grid; discard padding uniformly before barriers and bound linear arithmetic without JS shader rewriting. Remove when pinned WebGPU supports equivalent bounded dispatches.

Preserve once-only registry/device identity across lookup and own adapter/device callback results through wait failures. Never reset live counts, re-request admitted adapters, replace queues beneath buffers, retry automatically or publish late failed requests. Remove when upstream provides equivalent lifetime contracts.

Restore bounded Comfy GGUF original-shape metadata without changing payload, dtype, offsets or tensor elements; reject invalid, duplicate and conflicting shapes rather than bypassing validation through the generic parser. Remove when upstream preserves the same shape and validation contracts.

Backport upstream 4b1622afb BF16-left WebGPU matrix and row-lookup kernels while preserving existing binding, alignment and dispatch contracts. Remove when the image ggml pin supplies the equivalent kernels.

Bound WebGPU tensor writes and queue-wide pending uploads without changing tensor bytes, command order or completion ownership. Remove when upstream provides equivalent bounded upload and failure contracts.

Read eligible original BF16 device weights through bounded loader scratch without changing file bytes or offsets, retaining conversion and generic-reader fallbacks. Remove when upstream supplies equivalent checked, bounded reads and cleanup.

Retain explicitly registered original BF16 matrix/lookup weights on WebGPU with role, identity and allocation checks; preserve F32/F16, CPU and other roles. Remove when upstream supplies the same checked storage and fallback contract.

validation.browserSmokeScope: real-Wasm Worker, public records/callbacks, sparse GGUF/safetensors/shard I/O; test variants also check synthetic Qwen BF16 timestep and 3D convolution bias, bounded convolution/attention, softmax/RoPE, Qwen modulation/SwiGLU and cache-copy graph arithmetic on CPU (no GPU inference), plus large-row arithmetic and deep graph construction/selection (WebGPU mode also checks live-registry queries); no trained-model image generation
